solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruddy duck, colourful bird

parts.note: ruddy and flaming are both mild British intensifying expletives
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher identifies a ruddy duck, which is indeed a colourful bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddy duck is a real species, so the phrase reads as one bird; split it, and 'Ruddy' is the mild British curse FLAMING while a duck (a cricket score of nil) is O.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink wading bird is famously bright in plumage, hence a colourful bird.

clue.text: Frequently, when last of tequila is downed, that man can't stand

indicators.note: in a down clue, downed means moved further down the column

parts.note: a lot means frequently

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

parts.note: he refers to that man

explanation.surface: Whenever the last of the tequila gets drunk, that man can no longer stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is downed' moves a letter lower in the column: the A that ends 'tequila' slips two places down in A LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe someone is to detest them, so be unable to stand them.

clue.text: Without money, having moved across Atlantic?

parts.note: someone who has crossed the Atlantic from Britain is in the US

explanation.surface: An emigrant arrives penniless after crossing the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic and informally, minus means lacking, so a synonym of without.

clue.text: Self-regarding youth in car's thrown out South American

indicators.note: thrown out means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: US stands for American, as in US troops

explanation.surface: A vain youth is thrown out of a car belonging to a South American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges IN CARS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the beautiful young man who fell in love with his own reflection.

clue.text: Backing music in a group's somewhat structured

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read from right to left
somewhat means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A band's backing music sounds somewhat structured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes a run of letters from the words, and 'Backing' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic can mean systematically arranged, with parts forming a coordinated whole.

clue.text: Head having peeled off, kissing passionately

indicators.note: peeling something off strips its outer skin, so the outside letters of the word go

parts.note: snogging is British slang for kissing passionately

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head over a passionate kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having peeled off' removes the outer S and G of SNOGGING (British slang for kissing passionately).
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for the skull or the brain, as in 'use your noggin'.

clue.text: Fixes trouble separating partners

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A counsellor fixes the trouble that is splitting up a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' is the bridge pair North and South, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten or fix it in place.

clue.text: Punter to leave Red Lion disorientated

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: disorientated means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker staggers out of the Red Lion pub, disorientated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punter' suggests a pub customer or gambler; it is a boatman. 'disorientated' rearranges RED LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman propels his craft with a pole or oar, so a punter of sorts.

clue.text: Emphatically trendy suit

parts.note: in means fashionable
spades is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: A fashionable suit makes a strong statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing; it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning to a high degree, as in 'she has talent in spades'.

clue.text: Especially good knights succeeding each time in attack

indicators.note: succeeding here means taking the place of, so one set of letters replaces another

parts.note: to batter is to attack with repeated blows
T is the abbreviation for time, taken once for each occurrence, so both Ts
N is the chess notation for a knight, so two knights give NN

explanation.surface: A tale of knights who win every time they attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeding' means replacing: in BATTER the knights (N, N) take the place of each T (time).
explanation.definitionFit: North American adjective for outstandingly successful, as in a banner year for sales.

clue.text: Stout judge outside pub

indicators.note: outside tells us one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to judge an amount is to guess or estimate it
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A portly judge is seen standing outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' reads as an adjective describing the judge, but it is the Irish dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Irish brand is the best-known example of stout, the dark beer.

clue.text: Article, one penned by bridge player

parts.note: the definite article in English

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within, as if shut in a pen

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by a card player who plays bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge player' looks like one card-playing phrase; 'bridge' is SPAN and 'player' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player on stage, and the word comes from Thespis, the Greek father of drama.

clue.text: European dragging cleaner by the ear

indicators.note: playing by the ear means going by sound, so what is heard is taken rather than what is written

parts.note: a slow vac: dragging means slow, and a vac is a vacuum cleaner

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a vacuum cleaner along by its ear, as if it were a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragging cleaner' suggests pulling a cleaner along; it is a sluggish vacuum, a SLOW VAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Slovakia is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Brainless act, breaking instrument

indicators.note: breaking smashes the letters apart so they can be reassembled

explanation.surface: A mindless act of vandalism breaks a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges the letters of BRAINLESS ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pitched member of the clarinet family, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: An expression of triumph, seafood's elevated coastal city

indicators.note: elevated means raised, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: ole is the shout of triumph or approval at a bullfight
crab is a seafood

explanation.surface: A diner cheers on being served a towering seafood dish in a seaside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses AN OLE CRAB, read up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan capital lies on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Unbelievably daft perm, a problem of mine

indicators.note: unbelievably means in an implausible way, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone complains about an unbelievably daft perm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbelievably' rearranges DAFT PERM A; 'mine' is a coal mine, not 'belonging to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterdamp is the poisonous gas left in a coal pit after an explosion, a hazard of mining.

clue.text: After vacation in Scarborough, grim up north admits a dramatist

indicators.note: vacating a word empties it, leaving only its first and last letters
admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside
up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: dire means grim

explanation.surface: After a holiday in Scarborough, a playwright finds the north grim.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough is a seaside resort in Yorkshire. 'up' reverses the synonym for grim, read up the column, and 'admits' lets A in before N.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal, so a playwright.

clue.text: Gunman's device used by 10 aboard ship, Mary Rose

indicators.note: aboard puts something on the ship, so inside its letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the harp is the emblem on the stout brand in 10 across
Mary Rose is Cockney rhyming slang for nose, and a hooter is slang for a nose

explanation.surface: A gunman's emblem on board the Tudor warship Mary Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Rose looks like Henry VIII's warship; in Cockney rhyming slang (where a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with) it means nose, here HOOTER. 10 across is GUINNESS, whose logo is a harp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is a skilled marksman, a gunman who rarely misses.

clue.text: Cutting party, rising music writer went too far

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one piece goes into the other
rising in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: a do is a party
Verdi was the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer climbing the ladder cuts a party, overreaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses DO to OD, and VERDI cuts into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess.

clue.text: Bathroom's hot shower

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a bathroom; the 's stands for is
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A bathroom's hot shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is the verb, to give generously, not the bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish gifts on someone is to shower them with gifts.

clue.text: Pressing button led girl, disregarding the odds, to go crazy

indicators.note: going crazy scrambles the letters into a new order
ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: A girl pressing a button led her to go crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding the odds' takes the even letters of BUTTON LED GIRL, UTNEGR; 'to go crazy' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter demands immediate attention, as an urgent one does.

clue.text: Generously proportioned bath times

parts.note: a tub is a bath
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A capacious bath, used many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby is a gentle word for plump, stoutly built.

clue.text: International traveller has currency abroad, recalled grass

parts.note: the euro is the currency used in much of mainland Europe

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to grass or rat is British slang for informing on someone

explanation.surface: A traveller abroad with foreign currency remembers some grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses RATS (to grass, British slang for informing).
explanation.definitionFit: The train service running between London and the Continent through the Channel Tunnel, so an international traveller.

clue.text: Second vehicle's open-top, pathetic!

indicators.note: an open-top vehicle has lost its top, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a lorry is a British truck, the 's linking

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a second-hand open-top car as pathetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open-top' removes the top letter of LORRY, the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry can mean wretched or pitiful, as in a sorry state.

clue.text: Full of energy, tidy up odd bras accumulated on surface

indicators.note: full of means containing, so one part goes inside the other
tidying up rearranges things into a different order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone full of energy tidies up a pile of odd bras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidy up' rearranges ODD BRAS, and 'Full of' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, material that is adsorbed is held as a thin film on a surface rather than soaked in.

clue.text: Filling goods transporter, operator's larboard of vessel

indicators.note: filling means going inside something to fill it

parts.note: artic is British shorthand for an articulated lorry, a goods truck

indicators.note: larboard is the old nautical word for the left side, so the leftmost letter is taken

explanation.surface: A goods truck being loaded, its operator on the left side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARTIC is an articulated lorry, a large British truck; 'larboard of' gives the left-hand letter of 'operator's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the aorta, the main blood vessel leaving the heart.

clue.text: Edgy, like Rubik's cube?

definitions.meaning: the puzzle cube is notoriously hard, so it is not easy

explanation.surface: A Rubik's cube is edgy: it has lots of edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as UN-EASY, not easy, as the hard cube puzzle is; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy and anxious are synonyms; the cube puzzle is, cryptically, hard to do.

clue.text: Declines accepting tatty cloth borders for paintings

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the outer letters wrap around it

parts.note: dips means declines or falls

indicators.note: the borders of words are their outside letters

explanation.surface: A shop declines to accept tatty cloth borders for its paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes the outside letters of 'tatty' and 'cloth', and 'accepting' has the synonym for declines take them in; 'borders for paintings' looks like picture frames.
explanation.definitionFit: A diptych is a painting on two hinged panels, often an altarpiece.
